Subject: Solida Health — eval onboarding and dataset/score checklist

Hi Emily / Rajiv — thanks again for the 8:30 call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same plan: 

- Goal: run a Solida-specific model-fit evaluation on Redwood to validate triage + note-summarization quality before a short pilot. Primary success metric is label-level precision/recall on triage intents and ROUGE-L / human acceptability on summaries.
- Data: you agreed to a ~1k-sample representative subset (de-identified) for the first run. Preferred format is JSONL (see attachment).
- Recommended Redwood model(s): start with redwood-13b-qa-quant (best cost/quality tradeoff), fallback to redwood-7b-fp16 for latency-sensitive slices. Ben will provide rationale and scoring suggestion.
- Timeline: sample upload by EOD Tue (5/31), Redwood run Wed 6/1, internal recap with metrics Thu 6/2.
- Action items:
  1) Emily — upload sample JSONL to the Drive folder or share S3 link (per your security preference).
  2) Rajiv — confirm whether PII redaction is done or if you want Redwood to run our de-id pass (we quoted that in the SOW).
  3) Ben / Marissa — set up the eval job, attach scoring rubric and prompt sets, and confirm cost estimate.

Attachments: solida_eval_sample.jsonl (sample schema), solida_scoring_rubric_v1.pdf, redwood_eval_instructions.md

I'll mark this thread as the primary channel for coordination — feel free to reply inline so we keep a single timeline.

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Solida Health — eval onboarding and dataset/score checklist

Hi Emily / Rajiv — following up with recommended setup and scoring that will make the eval run high-signal and repeatable on Redwood. Short version up top, details below.

Short summary:
- Model recommendations: primary = redwood-13b-qa-quant (recommended because of token-efficiency and strong QA/summarization head); secondary = redwood-7b-fp16 for slices where latency is important (mobile/edge).
- Dataset format: JSONL, each record: {id, context, patient_note, gold_triage_label, gold_summary}. See sample attached.
- Scoring: automated for triage (micro/macro precision, recall, F1 at 12-label and aggregated 4-bucket), automated lexical metrics for summaries (ROUGE-L, BERTScore), and a human acceptability column for the 200-sample manual check. We will compute delta vs your current baseline model and flag regressions >5 pts absolute on key metrics.
- Eval config on Redwood: run with prefix caching enabled, batch size auto (we'll let the runtime choose), and produce per-sample outputs (for human review).

More detail (for your engineers):
1) JSONL schema (required fields): id (string), context (string - optional preamble from EHR), patient_note (string - the free text to summarize), gold_triage_label (string), gold_summary (string). Optional: metadata (free-form JSON string) but not required. See solida_eval_sample.jsonl.
2) Label mapping: provide mapping file for 12->4 buckets (we can accept a CSV or JSON mapping). If you supply only 12 labels, we will compute both granular and aggregated metrics ourselves.
3) Human review: supply a CSV with columns [id, rater_id, acceptability_score] for the 200 sample set; we will merge that to compute Spearman correlation vs automated metrics.
4) Security: if you prefer S3, provide a temporary presigned link; otherwise use the Drive folder. If you want Redwood to run de-id, confirm and we'll enable the pipeline (note: de-id may slightly change tokenization; we'll capture that in a run note).
5) Cost rough estimate: redwood-13b-qa-quant ~ $120 for the 1k run (token distribution assumption: avg 600 tokens per sample), redwood-7b-fp16 ~ $48 for the same run. These are estimates; final invoice will reflect exact token consumption.

I've attached the scoring rubric (solida_scoring_rubric_v1.pdf) and the sample JSONL. Marissa — can you provision the eval job on Wed morning and add Jordan as owner?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks — pinging to confirm operational details. On our side we'll: 

- Create an eval job named solida-hs23817-1 and stage it in the US host region.
- Use the supplied sample schema and run the two model configs sequentially (primary then fallback).
- Enable per-sample output + a zipped artifact with full predictions, per-sample metrics, and the run log.
- Add a regression alert: if any key metric drops >5 points vs provided baseline, send automated notification to your team and mine.

Emily: please drop the JSONL in the Drive folder (or share S3) and confirm de-id choice. If you upload to Drive, I'll pull via service account and delete temp copies after the job completes.

I'll schedule the run for Wed 2027-06-01 10:00 PDT, which gives your team time to upload and for us to validate schema on Tue night. If that works for you I'll lock it in and share the Redwood job link and cost-estimate card.
